deities: Twenty of the 24 Tirthankaras (tonks/shrines with their footprints mark nirvana sites)

history.dynasty: None (Jain tirtha; current temples rebuilt 1768 CE by Jagat Seth Mahtabchand; 1925-1933 additions)
history.period: One shrine dates to the 14th century; idol inscription 1678 CE; current structures 1768 CE onward; renovations in the 1980s
history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: this is a Jain tirtha (keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset). FLAG - DUPLICATE CSV ROW: 'Parasnath Temple' (seq 414) and 'Shikharji Temple' (seq 418) are the SAME complex - Shikharji/Sammed Shikharji is the name of the pilgrimage on Parasnath Hill, Jharkhand's highest peak (1,365-1,366 m). Twenty of the 24 Jain Tirthankaras attained nirvana here, including Parshvanatha (23rd), after whom the hill is named; some sources say all 24 are venerated here. The hill is dotted with tonks (shrines) marking each nirvana site; the summit temple is simple white marble. The site is shared by Digambara and Śvētāmbara sects. The 9 km uphill trek from Madhuban and the 27 km parikrama start at Palganj; the oldest structure is the ~300-year-old Bageecha Temple. The Santhal community calls the hill Marang Buru and holds a hunting festival on the Baisakh full moon.

name: Parasnath Temple (Sammed Shikharji)
town_description: Madhuban is the pilgrim base town at the foot of Parasnath Hill, about 25 km from Giridih, with dharamshalas, bhojnalayas, a Jain museum, and temples at the start of the 9 km uphill trek. (CSV town 'Giridih' is the district headquarters; corrected to Madhuban.)
tradition: Jainism (Digambara and Śvētāmbara) - NOT a Hindu temple; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Nearest airports are Ranchi (~190 km) and Kolkata; pilgrims usually travel via rail/road.
travel.railway: Parasnath railway station on the Grand Chord line is the nearest; Giridih and Madhupur are alternates.
travel.road: Madhuban is ~25 km from Giridih town; the summit is reached on foot (or doli) along a paved track, 9 km uphill from the base.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (cooler months for the trek); check pilgrimage season advisories.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temples generally open from early morning; summer timings reported as 4:00 AM to 6:00 PM (verify locally).
